items.title: Jefferies initiates coverage on Leela Hotels with Buy rating, sees 22% upside
items.description: Jefferies initiated coverage on Leela Hotels with a Buy rating and a Rs 675 target, citing India’s premiumisation trend, rising luxury travel demand and the company’s owned-led expansion strategy. The brokerage expects strong revenue and earnings growth through FY29, supported by higher room rates, leisure exposure and Brookfield backing.

items.title: Hindustan Zinc, Vedanta, Nalco and other metal stocks slide up to 5%. Here's why
items.description: Metal stocks tumbled up to 5% on Monday, with the Nifty Metal index falling over 2% amid a decline in metal prices and rising expectations of higher-for-longer US interest rates. Profit booking after the index’s strong August rally also weighed on sentiment, while Jefferies remained bullish on Hindustan Zinc over Hindalco.

items.title: Tejas Networks among 6 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: On August 28, six Nifty500 stocks that gained over 5% were identified using the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge.com. An uptrend signal is generated when the RSI value crosses above 50 from below. “RSI trending up” indicates that the Relative Strength Index (RSI) is rising, suggesting strengthening price momentum in the stock. This may signal potential upward movement and can be used by traders to identify buying opportunities.

items.title: Top Nifty50 stocks analysts suggest buying in this volatile week
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, is a comprehensive report that evaluates five key components of 4,000+ listed stocks – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum – to generate standardised scores. The simple average of the above-mentioned five component ratings is normally distributed to reach an average score.

items.title: Ashoka Buildcon shares rally 10% after securing Rs 602 crore order from RVNL
items.description: Ashoka Buildcon shares surged over 10% after the company received a Rs 602.16 crore order from Rail Vikas Nigam Limited for electro-mechanical works across four railway tunnels in Uttarakhand. The 30-month project is expected to strengthen the company’s order book, while the stock’s technical setup also remains in focus.

items.title: 20 stocks, 100% returns: How retail investors tapped a multibagger wave in deeper Indian market
items.description: Retail investors enjoyed impressive returns by picking specific stocks wisely. Over the last year, numerous companies showcased returns exceeding one hundred percent. Sectors like telecom and capital goods led the way, with high-beta and event-driven stocks also providing significant rewards. Ultimately, careful stock selection played a more vital role than merely concentrating on sector performance for achieving these gains.

items.title: HDFC Bank shares after Jagdishan: What lies ahead for the country’s largest private lender?
items.description: HDFC Bank's CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan plans to retire in October 2026 following a major merger, leaving investors eager for details on his successor and the bank's future direction. The institution encounters hurdles in attracting deposits and enhancing margins post-merger. Experts propose either a temporary internal leader or an external hire. In the meantime, stock performance may remain subdued until the next leadership is established.

items.title: ₹49 lakh crore market-cap wipeout! Are Nifty’s fallen giants bargains or value traps?
items.description: India's leading stocks have witnessed a staggering loss of forty-nine lakh crore rupees in total market capitalization. A significant decline has affected forty-seven companies within the Nifty index, with heavyweights like TCS, HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries, and Infosys leading the charge. Analysts are divided over whether these diminished stocks present enticing investment opportunities or merely serve as potential pitfalls.

items.title: Sensex falls 300 points, Nifty below 24,100 amid multiple headwinds. What lies ahead?
items.description: On Monday, Indian stock indices Sensex and Nifty dipped significantly, with broader market indices like Nifty Smallcap and Midcap also experiencing more severe declines. Major players like Infosys and Tata Steel were among those causing the downturn. In a contrasting trend, HDFC Bank shares managed to rise, reflecting an unusual market sentiment dominated by sellers, leading to more declining stocks than advances.

items.title: Lenskart shares to rally 40%? Nomura initiates coverage with Buy, says its growth journey has just started
items.description: Lenskart has emerged from challenger to market leader, with Nomura initiating coverage with a ‘Buy’ rating and Rs 888 target, implying around 40% upside. The brokerage sees a long growth runway driven by store expansion, strong market positioning, vertical integration and a cost advantage, while MSCI inclusion could also attract passive inflows.

items.title: HDFC Bank shares gain over 2% as CEO Jagdishan rejects new term; Morgan Stanley, Jefferies, others weigh in
items.description: HDFC Bank's Managing Director, Sashidhar Jagdishan, has opted against reappointment, prompting brokerages to uphold their positive stance on the bank's stock. In light of this announcement, the board has hastened efforts to find a suitable successor. Analysts appreciate this proactive approach as it alleviates concerns and promises potential value. Investors’ attention now shifts to the upcoming leadership transition and its expected impact on future growth prospects.

items.title: Ather Energy among 4 stocks flashing bullish signals, hinting at a possible uptrend
items.description: On August 28, four Nifty500 stocks that gained over 6% appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period, and the closing price is the highest.Represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and a small or nonexistent lower shadow, it indicates strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a signal that buyers were in control from the opening to the closing, often using such patterns for informed decisions about future price movements in financial markets.

items.title: Is Nifty set for a breakout? Analysts see signs of a shift ahead
items.description: Nifty hovered near 24,175, needing to clear 24,200 to regain strength. Analysts suggest bullish option spreads for rebounds and caution against a 23,900 break. HEG and Laurus Labs are recommended buys with specific targets and stop losses. Glenmark Pharmaceuticals and Shipping Corporation of India also present buying opportunities. Newgen Software and Elgi Equipments show positive chart setups for investors.

items.title: Augmont Enterprises shares debut at 22% premium over IPO price
items.description: The Rs 825 crore IPO, priced at Rs 788 per share, comprised a fresh issue of 79 lakh shares worth Rs 620 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 26 lakh shares aggregating Rs 205 crore. Ahead of the public issue, the company had also raised Rs 246.30 crore from anchor investors.

items.title: MSCI rebalancing threatens to turn ‘Messy’ in new Indian auction
items.description: This Monday marks a critical juncture for India's new closing auction system, as it gears up to manage an influx of billions in passive fund trades. The quarterly MSCI index rebalancing is expected to catalyze heightened trading volume, putting the system’s reliability under scrutiny. Both market participants and regulators are keenly awaiting how smoothly it addresses large institutional orders in this high-stakes environment.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 6 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, six stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200 DMA (Daily Moving Averages) on August 28, 2026, according to stockedge.com's technical scan data. The 200-day daily moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend in a particular stock. As long as the stock is priced above the 200-day SMA on the daily timeframe, it is generally considered to be in an overall uptrend. Take a look:

items.title: Market wrap: Sun Pharma, Nestle India, ITC, Adani Ports top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Monday
items.description: Indian benchmark indices ended lower on Monday, with the Sensex falling 307 points and the Nifty50 declining 0.39% amid rising US bond yields, crude oil prices and renewed rate-hike concerns. Adani Enterprises and Adani Ports led the losers, while Sun Pharma and Nestle India were among the top gainers.

items.title: Titan vs Kalyan Jewellers: Why HSBC favours both stocks amid jewellery sector growth
items.description: HSBC has picked Titan Company and Kalyan Jewellers as its preferred jewellery stocks, citing growth opportunities from daily-wear jewellery and B2B manufacturing. The brokerage has retained Buy ratings on both stocks, with target prices of Rs 5,550 and Rs 770, respectively, while highlighting key risks including gold price volatility and competition.

items.title: FIIs raised stakes in these 12 smallcap stocks in Q1; shares surge up to 123%
items.description: Tracking the activity of Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) can offer valuable investment insights, given that their decisions are typically backed by extensive research and analysis. In Q1, FIIs increased their holdings in around 532 BSE small-cap stocks compared with the previous quarter. Since the end of the June quarter—covering the period from early July to August 31, or roughly two months—most of these stocks have delivered decent returns. During this period, we highlight 11 small-cap stocks that have rallied between 50% and 125%. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Aurobindo Pharma gains over 3% as subsidiary launches generic Advair Diskus in US; stock up 41% YTD
items.description: Aurobindo Pharma shares rose sharply after its subsidiary Lannett Company launched the generic equivalent of Advair Diskus in the US. The inhalation product, available in two strengths, marks the first commercialised product from Aurobindo’s inhalation pipeline. The stock has gained 41.16% year-to-date in 2026.

items.title: Systematix initiates coverage on 5 affordable housing finance stocks; sees up to 48% upside
items.description: Systematix Research has initiated coverage of five affordable housing finance companies with Buy ratings, seeing 28-48% upside from current levels. The brokerage expects the sector to benefit from low mortgage penetration, rising incomes and urbanisation, with most covered companies projected to deliver loan growth in the low-to-mid-20% range through FY29.

items.title: Northern Arc Capital jumps 10% after Rs 335-crore block deal. Should you buy?
items.description: Northern Arc Capital shares surged after 1.21 crore shares changed hands in a large block deal during the morning session. The stock hit an intraday high of ₹315 and remained above its opening price and VWAP around noon, indicating that the early gains held through the session.

items.title: Why India’s new closing auction is agonising traders: Q&A
items.description: India’s new 20-minute closing auction system is facing renewed scrutiny after the Sensex briefly plunged nearly 3% during Thursday’s session, highlighting concerns over thin liquidity and price volatility. Introduced on August 3 to improve price discovery and align India with global markets, the system has also come under SEBI’s lens following an alleged market-manipulation case.

items.title: Explained: Why Jefferies prefers Kaynes Tech shares over Dixon Tech; urges caution on Syrma SGS
items.description: Jefferies prefers Kaynes Technology over Dixon Technologies as India pushes to deepen domestic electronics component manufacturing. The brokerage has a Buy rating on Kaynes Tech, while maintaining Hold calls on Dixon and Syrma SGS Technology. It expects stronger competition for mobile assembly players and advises caution on Syrma after its sharp rally.

items.title: Kaynes Tech, Wockhardt, Persistent Systems shares fall up to 5% as broader markets tumble. What lies ahead?
items.description: The stock market saw marked declines on Monday, particularly among smallcap and midcap shares. Persistent Systems and National Aluminium Company experienced prominent losses, contributing to the negative performance of the Nifty Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100 indices. Influenced by the Federal Reserve's remarks and increasing oil prices, investors are pivoting to prioritize growth opportunities over traditional value stocks.

items.title: G20, US Jobs Data, Rate Decisions: 5 key global market triggers this week
items.description: Global central bankers will move from Jackson Hole to Asheville, North Carolina, for the G20 meeting on Monday and Tuesday. Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda is expected to attend alongside Japan’s finance minister. Investors will closely watch discussions as geopolitics, elections and upcoming interest-rate decisions create uncertainty. The Fed and BOJ meetings in September are already emerging as key risk events, while Middle East tensions, France’s budget negotiations and Germany’s regional elections remain on the radar. (Source: Reuters)

items.title: Stock picks of the week: 5 stocks with consistent score improvement and upside potential of up to 24%
items.description: US bond yields remain elevated, suggesting that the debt market expects inflation to move up. Now, if the risk-free returns indicated by the yield on US bonds stays high, it means that flows to emerging markets will be lower. However, this is likely to be a short-term thing; we have seen this happening in the past as well.Our selected stocks for today depict a strong upward trajectory in their overall average score which is based on five key pillars: Earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum. This implies that there has been a significant improvement in their market outlook in the given time frame.

items.title: Jefferies cuts HDFC Bank share price target but retains Buy after CEO opts out of new term. Here’s why
items.description: Jefferies retained its Buy rating on HDFC Bank but cut the target price to Rs 880 from Rs 1,050 following CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan’s decision not to seek reappointment. The brokerage flagged near-term risks to deposit mobilisation and fee income but said valuations remain undemanding.

items.title: Transformers and Rectifiers shares rally 8% after receiving order worth up to  Rs 500 crore from MEIL
items.description: Transformers and Rectifiers shares rallied on Monday after the company secured a large order from MEIL for manufacturing transformers and related work. Valued at Rs 100 crore to Rs 500 crore, excluding GST, the order is scheduled for execution over 35 months and is expected to strengthen the company’s order pipeline.

items.title: Zee Entertainment shares crash 14% amid Subhash Chandra’s 99.97% loan haircut row
items.description: Zee Entertainment shares crashed on Monday after the NCLT approved a repayment plan involving founder Subhash Chandra. The plan entails a recovery of around Rs 6.5 crore against admitted creditor claims of Rs 22,006.57 crore, implying a 99.97% haircut.

items.title: Augmont Enterprises shares drop 2% after listing at 22% premium. Buy, sell or hold the stock?
items.description: Augmont Enterprises made a strong stock market debut, listing at a 22% premium to its IPO price, but gains fell short of grey market expectations. With valuations considered rich, brokerages have offered mixed views, ranging from Neutral to Subscribe for Long Term. Investors will weigh the company’s growth prospects, margins, integrated precious-metals ecosystem and key risks.

items.title: IGL shares jump 3% after CNG price hike in Delhi NCR. What lies ahead?
items.description: IGL shares witnessed an uptick on Monday after the company hiked CNG prices by Rs 3.89 per kg in Delhi-NCR, citing higher imported LNG costs. The increase marks the fifth price hike this year. Citi retained its Buy rating on IGL, saying the latest hike could improve realisations and support margins.
